To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a tris(phosphinamide)zirconium complex has been shown for the first time to activate hydrazine N-H bonds, and this reactivity is promoted by the presence of a redox-active cobalt atom in the heterobimetal complex.
a Zr-Co complex promotes one-electron reactivity of the Zr center, and that the Co atom can act as a redox mediator.
the heterobimetalic complex [CpZr(NH2)(NC5H4)]Co(CO)2 (Cp = eta5-C5H5) promotes the one-electron oxidation of the Zr-NH2 bond of hydrazinyl ligands via a proton-coulped electron transfer mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization and reactivity of transition metal complexes.
the synthesis of new metal complexes and their use in catalysis, in particular for the activation and functionalization of small molecules.

the design, preparation, and characterization of molecular complexes and materials that exhibit unique reactivity and properties, and that have the potential to impact the fields of chemical synthesis, catalysis, energy, materials science, and biology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heterobimetalic complex is able to activate N-H bond of hydrazide and hydrazine via a proton-couple electron transfer (PCET) process.
the heterobimetalic Zr-Co complex 2 is able to activate hydrazine N-H bonds via an unprecedented proton-coupled-electron transfer mechanism.
the Co atom in this complex promotes the one-electron reactivity at the Zr center.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Zr-Co heterometallic system can be used to activate N-H bond of hydrazide derivatives.

the heterobimetal complex can activate N-H bonds by a one-electron process, while a homobimetallic analogue can only achieve this by a two-electron process, and the monomeric analogue cannot achieve this at all.
a heterobimelatic complex is a powerful tool for promoting one-electron reactivity at Zr, and the Zr-Co bond is a key component in this reactivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a redox active metal can promote unusual chemistry at an early metal, which is otherwise not possible.
the presence of a second metal in the coordination sphere of a metal center can have a profound effect on the chemical reactivity.
